france/cremant-de-bourgogne.text: A Burgundy appellation for quality sparkling wine, made from Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Gamay, Aligoté and several other grapes. Its area covers hundreds of communes, including Chablis, Beaune and Beaujeu.

france/cremant-de-die.text: A Rhône Valley appellation for quality sparkling wine made from Clairette, Aligoté and Muscat à Petits Grains.

france/cremant-de-limoux.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for quality sparkling wine in which Chardonnay is the main grape. Chenin, Mauzac and Pinot Noir are also allowed, across about 40 communes around Limoux in the Aude.

france/cremant-de-loire.text: A Loire Valley appellation for quality sparkling wine made from Chenin, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc and several other grapes.

france/cremant-du-jura.text: A Jura appellation for quality sparkling wine made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Poulsard, Trousseau and Savagnin Blanc, across 96 communes. Jura is a cool-climate region between Burgundy and Switzerland, best known for vin jaune.

france/criots-batard-montrachet.text: A Côte de Beaune appellation in Burgundy, within Chassagne-Montrachet, for white wine made only from Chardonnay. The village of Chassagne-Montrachet makes about two-thirds white and one-third red wine.

france/crozes-hermitage.text: The largest appellation of the northern Rhône, making mostly red wine from Syrah, sometimes blended with a little Marsanne or Roussanne. Some white wine is made from Marsanne and Roussanne. Its wines are less highly regarded than Hermitage or Côte-Rôtie.

france/cuis.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/cumieres.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/dizy.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/ecueil.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/grauves.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/hautvillers.text: A cru village in the Vallée de la Marne, a Champagne sub-region. Its sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/jouy-les-reims.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/le-mesnil-sur-oger.text: A cru village in the Côte des Blancs, a Champagne sub-region whose vineyards are 95% Chardonnay. Champagne's sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/les-mesneux.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/louvois.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region with chalk-based soils and nine Grands Crus villages. Champagne's sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/ludes.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/mailly-champagne.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region with chalk-based soils and nine Grands Crus villages. Champagne's sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/mareuil-sur-ay.text: A cru village in the Vallée de la Marne, a Champagne sub-region with variable soils. Champagne's sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/montbre.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/etrechy.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes such as Petit Meslier, Arbane and Pinot Blanc.

france/drome.text: A French regional (PGI) designation for wines of the Drôme, where Grenache (38%) and Syrah (33%) are planted most. Muscat Blanc, Carignan and Merlot follow far behind.

france/echezeaux.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation in Burgundy, within Vougeot, for red wine made from Pinot Noir. Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris are also allowed in small amounts.

france/entraygues-le-fel.text: A South West France appellation of eight communes, making wine from Fer for red and Chenin for white. Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and a few other grapes are allowed too.

france/entre-deux-mers.text: The largest sub-region of Bordeaux, between the Garonne and Dordogne rivers, with about 3,700 acres in vine. Its wines are made from Semillon, Sauvignon and Muscadelle, plus red grapes such as Merlot and Cabernet Franc.

france/estaing.text: A South West France appellation of three communes, making wine from Gamay, Fer and Chenin. A long list of other grapes, including Cabernet Franc, Merlot and Pinot Noir, is allowed in smaller amounts.

france/faugeres.text: A Languedoc appellation in the foothills of the Massif Central north of Béziers. Its wines are made from Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Lledoner Pelut for red, and Marsanne, Roussanne, Vermentino and Grenache Blanc for white.

france/fiefs-vendeens.text: A Loire Valley appellation in the Vendée. Its wines are made from Cabernet Franc, Gamay and Pinot Noir for red, and Chardonnay, Chenin and Sauvignon for white.

france/fitou.text: A large Languedoc appellation for red wine in which Carignan is the dominant grape, at least 40% of the blend. Grenache, Mourvèdre and Syrah are blended with it.

france/fixin.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation in Burgundy. About 96% of the wine is red from Pinot Noir, with a little white from Chardonnay. It has no Grand Cru vineyards.

france/fleurie.text: A Beaujolais appellation for red wine made from Gamay, with Aligoté, Chardonnay and Melon allowed in small amounts.

france/floc-de-gascogne.text: A South West France appellation for liqueur wine, covering 282 communes. A long list of grapes is allowed, including Colombard, Gros Manseng, Ugni Blanc, Merlot and Tannat.

france/fronsac.text: A Bordeaux appellation on the Right Bank of the Gironde estuary, making red wine only. It is based mostly on Merlot, with Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Canon Fronsac lies entirely inside it.

france/fronton.text: A South West France appellation north of Toulouse, built on the red grape Négrette. Cabernet Franc, Syrah, Gamay and several other grapes are allowed alongside it.

france/gaillac.text: A South West France appellation in the Tarn, making still and sparkling wines. Its main grapes are Mauzac, Len de l'El and Ondenc for white, and Fer, Duras and Prunelard for red, plus Syrah and Gamay.

france/gaillac-premieres-cotes.text: A South West France appellation of 11 communes around Gaillac, for white wine. It is made from Mauzac, Len de l'El, Ondenc and Muscadelle, plus Sauvignon.

france/gers.text: A French regional (PGI) designation for wines of the Gers. Colombard (34%) is the most planted grape, then Sauvignon Blanc, Gros Manseng and Ugni Blanc. Tannat is the leading red.

france/gevrey-chambertin.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation for red wine made from Pinot Noir. It holds nine Grand Cru vineyards, Chambertin and eight others, and has many village-level vineyards, since it stretches far east.

france/gigondas.text: A southern Rhône appellation in the commune of Gigondas, mainly for red wine from Grenache, with a little rosé. White wine was added in 2022. It is seen as a little brother to Châteauneuf-du-Pape and can age well.

france/givry.text: A Côte Chalonnaise appellation in Burgundy. Almost 80% of its wine is red, from Pinot Noir, and the rest is white, from Chardonnay. It has 27 Premier Cru vineyards and no Grand Cru.

france/grand-auxerrois.text: A Burgundy area in the Yonne that holds three appellations: Saint-Bris, Vézelay and Irancy.

france/grand-roussillon.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for liqueur wine, covering 98 communes. It is made from Grenache in its red, white and gray forms, plus Macabeu and two Muscats.

france/grands-echezeaux.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation in Burgundy, within Vougeot, for red wine made from Pinot Noir. Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris are also allowed in small amounts.

france/graves.text: A Bordeaux sub-region on the left bank of the Garonne, with red and white wines, mostly red. Reds blend Cabernet and Merlot, and whites use Sauvignon, Semillon and Muscadelle. The name means gravelly land.

france/graves-de-vayres.text: A Bordeaux appellation for red and white wine, about 1,700 acres in two communes inside Entre-Deux-Mers. Reds use Merlot and Cabernets, whites use Sauvignon, Semillon and Muscadelle.

france/graves-superieures.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation across 42 communes. Its wines are made from Sauvignon, Semillon and Muscadelle for white, with Merlot and the Cabernets also allowed.

france/grignan-les-adhemar.text: A Rhône Valley appellation in the Drôme, across 21 communes. Its wines are made from Syrah, Grenache and Cinsaut for red, and Grenache Blanc, Marsanne, Roussanne and Viognier for white.

france/griotte-chambertin.text: A Grand Cru in Gevrey-Chambertin, in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine from Pinot Noir. It lies on the lower side of the Route des Grands Crus, and its name comes from the grill pan shape of the vine rows.

france/gros-plant-du-pays-nantais.text: A Loire Valley appellation in the Loire-Atlantique for white wine made from Folle Blanche. Colombard and Montils are also allowed, across 68 communes.

france/haut-medoc.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation along about 37 miles of the Médoc, for red wine. It is based on Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, with Cabernet Franc and others. Six other appellations sit inside it, including Pauillac and Saint-Julien.

france/haut-montravel.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France, covering 13 communes in the Dordogne. It makes white wine from Sauvignon, Semillon and Muscadelle, with Ondenc allowed too.

france/haut-poitou.text: A Loire Valley appellation of 24 communes, with Sauvignon for white and Cabernet Franc for red. Gamay, Merlot and Pinot Noir are also allowed.

france/hautes-cotes-de-beaune.text: A Burgundy sub-region on top of and behind the Côte de Beaune escarpment, in valleys and slopes. Its one appellation covers red and rosé from Pinot Noir and white from Chardonnay. It has no Premier Cru vineyards.

france/hautes-cotes-de-nuits.text: A Burgundy sub-region on top of and behind the Côte de Nuits escarpment, in valleys and slopes. Its one appellation covers red and rosé from Pinot Noir and white from Chardonnay. It has no Premier Cru vineyards.

france/hermitage.text: A northern Rhône appellation on a hill south of Lyon, making mostly red wine from Syrah. Small amounts of white are made from Roussanne and Marsanne. Some see the hill as the spiritual home of Syrah.

france/irancy.text: A Burgundy appellation in the Grand Auxerrois, in the Yonne, for red wine made from Pinot Noir and César across three communes. Pinot Gris is also allowed.

france/irouleguy.text: A South West France appellation, the only one in the Northern Basque Country and often called the smallest vineyard in France. About 70% of the wine is red, with Tannat and Cabernet Franc, plus 20% rosé and 10% white from Manseng and Courbu.

france/jasnieres.text: A Loire Valley appellation for white wine made only from Chenin, across two communes.

france/julienas.text: A Beaujolais cru for red wine made from Gamay, and the most northerly of the ten crus. It sits on the north bank of the Mauvaise valley and is said to take its name from Julius Caesar.

france/jura.text: A cool-climate region between Burgundy and Switzerland, with distinctive wines. Its best-known style is vin jaune, made from Savagnin under a flor-like yeast, alongside Poulsard, Trousseau and Chardonnay, vin de paille, Crémant du Jura and Macvin.

france/jurancon.text: A South West appellation in the Pyrenees foothills, making dry white wine and a more sought-after sweet white. Both come from Petit Manseng and Gros Manseng on steep slopes, with tropical aromas such as pineapple and mango in the sweet wines.

france/l-etoile.text: A Jura appellation of four communes, making wine from Savagnin Blanc and Chardonnay, with Poulsard also allowed. Its types include wine from raisined grapes. Jura is a cool-climate region best known for vin jaune.

france/la-clape.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation of six communes. Its red wines use Mourvèdre, Syrah and Grenache, and its whites use Clairette, Grenache Blanc, Marsanne, Roussanne, Vermentino and others.

france/la-grande-rue.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation in Burgundy, within Vosne-Romanée. It allows Pinot Noir for red and Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris for white.

france/la-liviniere.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation of six communes, for red wine made from Syrah, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Lledoner Pelut. Carignan and Cinsaut are also allowed.

france/la-romanee.text: A Grand Cru in Vosne-Romanée, in the Côte de Nuits, for red wine from Pinot Noir. It is a monopole of Comte Liger-Belair, and its AOC dates from 1936.

france/la-tache.text: A Grand Cru in Vosne-Romanée, in the Côte de Nuits, for red wine from Pinot Noir. It is a monopole of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, and its AOC dates from 1936.

france/ladoix.text: A Côte de Beaune appellation, about three-quarters red from Pinot Noir and one-quarter white from Chardonnay. Part of the Corton hill lies in the commune, including Grand Cru vineyards of Corton and Corton-Charlemagne.

france/lalande-de-pomerol.text: A Bordeaux Right Bank appellation for red wine, just north of Pomerol across the Barbanne stream. It is made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cot, and its main villages are Lalande-de-Pomerol and Néac.

france/languedoc.text: A large southern appellation across 527 communes, with Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Lledoner Pelut as main red grapes and a long list of whites. The Hérault and Aude grow mostly Syrah (17%), Merlot, Grenache and Carignan.

france/languedoc-roussillon.text: A large wine region on the Mediterranean coast of southern France. It includes Pic Saint-Loup, Faugères, Minervois, Corbières, Fitou and Limoux.

france/latricieres-chambertin.text: A Grand Cru in Gevrey-Chambertin, in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine from Pinot Noir. Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris are also allowed.

france/left-bank.text: A Bordeaux area taking in Médoc, Graves and appellations such as Pauillac, Margaux, Saint-Julien, Saint-Estèphe and Pessac-Léognan.

france/les-baux-de-provence.text: A Provence appellation of seven communes. Reds use Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Cinsaut, and whites use Grenache Blanc, Vermentino and Clairette.

france/limoux.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation around Limoux, covering sparkling and still wines. Mauzac, Chardonnay and Chenin are used for whites, and Merlot mostly for reds. Wine historians believe the first sparkling wine was made here in 1531.

france/lirac.text: A southern Rhône appellation in the Gard, on the right bank of the Rhône, one of the 13 Rhône crus. It borders Tavel, and its wines use Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah and Cinsaut for red, and Clairette and Grenache Blanc for white.

france/listrac-medoc.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation in a single commune, for red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and others.

france/loire-valley.text: The wine regions along the Loire river, from Muscadet on the Atlantic coast to Sancerre in the east.

france/loupiac.text: A Bordeaux appellation in Entre-Deux-Mers, the largest Bordeaux sub-region, between the Garonne and Dordogne rivers. Loupiac covers one commune and makes white wine from Semillon, Sauvignon and Muscadelle.

france/luberon.text: A Rhône Valley appellation at the southeastern edge of the region, in Provence, with 36 communes in the Vaucluse. Known as Côtes du Luberon until 2009, it is made from Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre for red, and Clairette, Grenache Blanc, Marsanne, Roussanne and Vermentino for white.

france/lussac-saint-emilion.text: A Bordeaux Right Bank appellation in one commune, for red wine made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cot.

france/macon.text: A Burgundy appellation of 89 communes, for red wine from Gamay and Pinot Noir and white wine from Chardonnay.

france/macon-villages.text: A Burgundy appellation in the Mâconnais, which is best known for good-value white wine from Chardonnay.

france/maconnais.text: The southern part of Burgundy, west of the Saône, best known for good-value white wine from Chardonnay. Pouilly-Fuissé is particularly sought after. Nearly all of its wine is white.

france/macvin-du-jura.text: A Jura appellation for liqueur wine across 96 communes. It can be made from red grapes such as Pinot Noir, Poulsard and Trousseau, and white such as Chardonnay and Savagnin Blanc.

france/madiran.text: A South West appellation of about 3,200 acres, spread over three départements and built on red Tannat, with Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Fer. White Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh comes from the same area.

france/malepere.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation of 39 communes for red and rosé wine, led by Merlot and Cabernet Franc. Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cinsaut and Grenache are also allowed.

france/maranges.text: A Côte de Beaune appellation in three communes. About 95% of its wine is red from Pinot Noir, and the rest white from Chardonnay. It has no Grand Cru vineyards.

france/marcillac.text: A South West France appellation near Rodez in the Aveyron, for red and rosé wine made from Fer. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Prunelard are also allowed.

france/margaux.text: A Bordeaux appellation within Haut-Médoc, for red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and others. It has 21 cru classé châteaux, more than any other commune in Bordeaux.

france/marsannay.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation, the only village appellation allowed to make rosé. Red wine, about two-thirds of production, and rosé use Pinot Noir, and white uses Chardonnay. It has no Grand Cru or Premier Cru vineyards.

france/maury.text: A Roussillon appellation for fortified vin doux naturel, almost all red, made from at least 75% Grenache Noir. It is made and marketed much like port, with spirit added.

france/mazis-chambertin.text: A Grand Cru in Gevrey-Chambertin, in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine from Pinot Noir. It lies above the Route des Grands Crus, closest to the town of Gevrey-Chambertin of the Chambertin vineyards.

france/mazoyeres-chambertin.text: A Grand Cru in Gevrey-Chambertin, in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine from Pinot Noir. It lies below the Route des Grands Crus, and its AOC dates from 1937.

france/medoc.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation on the northern Médoc peninsula, sometimes called Bas-Médoc. It makes almost only red wine, from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and others.

france/menetou-salon.text: An appellation of ten communes, making white from Sauvignon and red from Pinot Noir.

france/mercurey.text: A Côte Chalonnaise appellation in Burgundy. Almost 80% of its wine is red, from Pinot Noir, and the rest is white, from Chardonnay. It has 32 Premier Cru vineyards and no Grand Cru.

france/meursault.text: A Côte de Beaune appellation, about 98% white from Chardonnay, with a little red from Pinot Noir. It has no Grand Cru vineyards but several highly regarded Premier Cru vineyards.

france/minervois.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation across 60 communes, in the Aude and Hérault. Its reds must be blended from at least two grapes, led by Syrah, Mourvèdre, Grenache and Lledoner Pelut.

france/monbazillac.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France, across the Dordogne from the town of Bergerac, for sweet white wine made from Semillon, Sauvignon and Muscadelle. It covers almost 4,900 acres.

france/montagne-de-reims.text: One of the five Champagne sub-regions, around Reims Mountain between Reims and Épernay, with nine Grand Cru villages. Its soils are chalk-based and Pinot Noir is the main grape.

france/montagne-saint-emilion.text: A Bordeaux appellation on the Right Bank of the Dordogne, making only red wine from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cot. It covers about 3,700 acres.

france/montagny.text: A Côte Chalonnaise appellation in Burgundy, for white wine made only from Chardonnay, across four communes. It has 49 Premier Cru vineyards and no Grand Cru.
